ASReview LAB.summary: ASReview LAB (Utrecht University) is an Apache-2.0 active-learning tool for title/abstract screening; all facts below were fetched 2026-09-02. Current release is v3.0.8 (GitHub release 2026-06-18; PyPI 3.0.8, requires Python >=3.10; repo last pushed 2026-08-31; GitHub API license spdx Apache-2.0). It ingests only exported reference files (RIS/CSV/XLSX/TSV from citation managers and search engines such as Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, OpenAlex; PubMed export marked not supported) and does no query building, full-text retrieval, metadata verification, drafting, claim checking, quotation, or manuscript auditing. Screening decisions are fully persisted: exports add asreview_label, asreview_time, asreview_note, asreview_user_name/email plus tags, and the .asreview project file "contains the dataset, review history, notes, and model configuration" (manage.html). Citation-network support is limited to the separate asreview-datatools extension's OpenAlex forward/backward snowballing, and PyPI shows asreview-datatools 1.4 (2025-02-06) requires "asreview<2,>=1.1", so it is not compatible with LAB v3 — hence "partial". Deployment: pip, Docker image ghcr.io/asreview/asreview, or the self-hosted ASReview LAB Server / Server Stack (Docker Compose, PostgreSQL, NGINX, MIT-licensed; https://asreview.readthedocs.io/en/latest/server/overview.html and https://github.com/asreview/asreview-server-stack); docs mention no API keys or GPU. Empirical validation: Nat Mach Intell 2021 simulation studies report WSS@95 average 83% (67-92%), 95% of eligible studies found after screening 8-33%, RRF@10% 70-100% (verbatim from the Nature article HTML); follow-up Ferdinands et al. 2023 Systematic Reviews 12, DOI 10.1186/s13643-023-02257-7 (Crossref-verified) reports WSS@95 63.9-91.7% and recall@10% 53.6-99.8% across six datasets; the SYNERGY benchmark (DataCite-verified DOI 10.34894/HE6NAQ, 2023; https://github.com/asreview/synergy-dataset) comprises 26 systematic reviews and 169,288 records, CC0. Unverified: asreview.nl homepage content (redirect target of asreview.ai; fetch failed twice), and the absence of GPU/API-key requirements is inferred from docs omission rather than an explicit statement.

litstudy.summary: litstudy (Netherlands eScience Center; Heldens et al., SoftwareX 20:101207, 2022, DOI 10.1016/j.softx.2022.101207, Crossref- and OpenAlex-verified 2026-09-02) is an Apache-2.0 Python/Jupyter library for metadata-level bibliometrics, not a retrieval-augmented review or drafting system. Sources (README and litstudy/sources/__init__.py, fetched 2026-09-02): live search of Scopus (via pybliometrics, requires subscription + Elsevier API key), Semantic Scholar, CrossRef, DBLP and arXiv, plus import of IEEE Xplore/Springer Link CSV exports, BibTeX, RIS and generic CSV. Core capabilities are DocumentSet set-algebra/dedup/filter, statistics plots, citation/co-citation/bibliographic-coupling/co-author networks (networkx + pyvis), and NMF/LDA topic modelling over title/abstract bags-of-words. It has no query-refinement aid (users pass raw database query strings), no screening workflow or persisted inclusion/exclusion decisions (filter_docs simply returns a new DocumentSet from a predicate), and the paper explicitly states 'litstudy only works on metadata, it does not fetch or have access to the content of documents', so full-text acquisition, grounded drafting, claim-to-source checking, verbatim evidence quotation and manuscript auditing are all absent; a grep of the package source (fetched 2026-09-02) found no pdf/fulltext/LLM code. The closest analogue to metadata verification is 'refinement' (refine_crossref/refine_scopus/refine_semanticscholar), which re-fetches records by DOI (or fuzzy title for Scopus) and splits found vs. not-found sets, but does not diff or flag discrepancies. Validation in the paper is an illustrative GPU-programming case (1,441 IEEE+Springer records, 1,387 matched on Scopus, 53 discarded, 1,386 after year filter; 15 NMF topics; Big Data share 14% in 2011 to 26% in 2021) plus an impact narrative (prior use in an ACM Computing Surveys exascale survey, 23 stars/11 forks in June 2022); no precision/recall or user-study numbers are published. Current state (GitHub API and PyPI JSON, 2026-09-02): 221 stars, 67 forks, last push 2025-05-27, latest PyPI release 1.0.6 (2023-10-05), requires_python >=3.7; no GPU requirement is documented anywhere. The paper itself notes that supporting a complete systematic review 'is not the primary goal of litstudy'.

PaperQA2.summary: PaperQA2 (Future-House/paper-qa, Apache-2.0, PyPI version 2026.8.12, ~9.1k GitHub stars, last push 2026-08-26) is an open-source agentic RAG library/CLI for question answering over a user-supplied corpus of scientific PDFs. All facts below were fetched on 2026-09-02 from the GitHub README (raw + rendered), LICENSE, src/paperqa/prompts.py, src/paperqa/types.py, src/paperqa/clients/__init__.py, docs/tutorials/where_do_I_get_papers.md, the GitHub/PyPI/arXiv/DataCite/Crossref/OpenAlex APIs, and the arXiv HTML of 2409.13740v2. Interpretation of the 'supported' flag: whether PaperQA2 supports the criterion (yes/partial/no), with 'unverified' reserved for items I could not check. Key findings for the comparison with ScholarRAG: (1) Data sources: local PDFs are the corpus; metadata is enriched via Crossref, Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, Unpaywall, plus journal-quality and retraction post-processors (clients/__init__.py ALL_CLIENTS); optional Zotero and OpenReview helpers exist in paperqa.contrib. (2) Query refinement is agent-internal ('LLM-generated keyword query', 'iteratively refine queries and answers'), not a user-facing research-question refinement aid. (3) No title/abstract screening workflow and no screening audit trail: relevance is decided per text chunk by an LLM 0-10 score (irrelevant = empty summary, score 0); the only paper-level selection is the OpenReview helper. (4) Citation-network analysis: the paper describes a 'Citation Traversal' tool using Semantic Scholar and Crossref for references and citers, but the README FAQ states it is internal to FutureHouse and not yet in the repo. (5) Full-text acquisition: the README says 'you will need to provide PDFs yourself'; the paper says the open-source paper-search tool is a stub; Unpaywall only supplies OA links. (6) Grounded drafting: the QA prompt restricts citations to retrieved context keys and types.py strips 'hallucinated citations'; WikiCrow generates Wikipedia-style cited articles (answer/article level, not manuscript sections). (7) Metadata verification applies to ingested documents (title/DOI inferred then resolved via Crossref etc., with retraction check), not to an externally drafted reference list. (8) Claim verification is contradiction detection (contracrow setting: query is a claim to check against the literature), not checking a drafted claim against its cited source. (9) Evidence is returned as LLM 'contextual summaries' (~100 words) that are instructed to include direct quotes in quotation marks; the raw chunk text is retained in Context.text but the primary output is a summary, not verbatim excerpts. (10) External manuscript auditing: the paper's ContraCrow pipeline extracts claims from a provided paper and checks each for contradictions (2.34 +/- 1.99 per paper, 70% human-validated, F1 0.82), but claim extraction is not exposed in the OSS repo and there is no reference-list audit. (11) Deployment: pip install paper-qa (Python >=3.11), any LiteLLM-compatible model via API key or local llama.cpp/Ollama, optional CROSSREF_API_KEY / SEMANTIC_SCHOLAR_API_KEY; GPU requirements are not mentioned (unverified). (12) Empirical validation (arXiv 2409.13740v2): LitQA2 248 questions, precision 85.2% +/- 1.1% and accuracy 66.0% +/- 1.2% vs human experts 73.8% +/- 9.6% precision and 67.7% +/- 11.9% accuracy (n=9); WikiCrow 240 gene articles with 13.5% vs 24.9% 'cited and unsupported' statements vs Wikipedia (p=0.0075) and 3.9x fewer uncited statements; ContraCrow 2.34 +/- 1.99 contradictions/paper (N=93), 70% validated. Canonical citation: Skarlinski et al., 'Language agents achieve superhuman synthesis of scientific knowledge', arXiv:2409.13740 (2024), DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2409.13740 registered with DataCite; Crossref returns 404 for this DOI and neither Crossref bibliographic search nor OpenAlex shows a peer-reviewed journal version as of 2026-09-02, so crossref_verified=false (arXiv/DataCite-verified instead). The GitHub API reports a 'homepage' field of https://futurehouse.gitbook.io/futurehouse-cookbook, which I did not fetch (unverified); the GitHub repository is used as the homepage.

Ai2 Scholar QA.summary: Ai2 Scholar QA (Allen Institute for AI) is an Apache-2.0 open-source RAG pipeline and web app for long-form scientific question answering: it decomposes the query with an LLM, retrieves up to 256 passages + 20 abstracts from Semantic Scholar's 11.7M-paper full-text snippet index and 100M+ abstract index, reranks with mxbai-rerank-large-v1 (top 50), extracts verbatim quotes per paper, clusters them into a thematic outline, and generates a multi-section report with inline citations linked to excerpt popups plus paper-comparison tables. Verified strengths as a comparator: exact evidence quotation (yes), cited drafting (partial, since 'LLM Memory' uncited content is explicitly allowed), automatic query decomposition (partial), and published benchmark results (ScholarQA-CS total 61.9 vs STORM 59.5, OpenScholar 53.5, PaperQA2 51.4; ALCE-style citation score 48.1; 30.2k queries from 8,219 visitors over 9 weeks, 85% positive of 2,433 thumbs; ~$0.50 and 2.5 min per report). Verified gaps vs ScholarRAG: no human title/abstract screening workflow or exportable per-record exclusion log (only JSON pipeline traces), no citation-network analytics (one-hop citation following only), no OA PDF acquisition (relies on S2ORC pre-indexed passages), no Crossref/DOI metadata verification, no in-pipeline claim-to-source entailment check (users verify by clicking excerpts; entailment used only in offline evaluation), and no import/audit of an external manuscript (input is a query string). Deployment: self-hostable via Docker Compose or pip, requires S2_API_KEY plus Anthropic and/or OpenAI keys (any litellm provider), reranker served on Modal GPU (production: one NVIDIA L40S) or locally via sentence-transformers. Canonical citation is Crossref-verified: Singh et al., ACL 2025 System Demonstrations, pp. 513-523, DOI 10.18653/v1/2025.acl-demo.49 (arXiv 2504.10861v2); note Crossref/ACL list 9 authors while arXiv and the README BibTeX list 18. Both legacy demo URLs (qa.allen.ai, scholarqa.allen.ai) now redirect to asta.allen.ai/synthesize. All URLs accessed 2026-09-02; the Ai2 blog post (https://allenai.org/blog/ai2-scholarqa, Jan 21 2025) was also fetched and contains no benchmark numbers.

OpenScholar.summary: OpenScholar (Ai2 + UW) is an open retrieval-augmented LM that answers scientific queries with citation-backed long-form syntheses. All facts below were verified on 2026-09-02. Canonical citation: the arXiv preprint 2411.14199 (v1 2024-11-21, arXiv API) was published in Nature 650(8103):857-863, online 2026-02-04, DOI 10.1038/s41586-025-10072-4 (Crossref journal-article record fetched; PMID 41639446 via E-utilities; OpenAlex W7127589252). Note the title changed (no 'OpenScholar:' prefix) and the author list grew from 25 to 28; the GitHub/HF BibTeX still cite arXiv. Architecture (Nature full text, fetched via curl since WebFetch hit an idp.nature.com redirect): datastore OSDS = peS2o v3 (open-access S2ORC papers, 45M papers to Oct 2024, 236M passages), plus Semantic Scholar keyword API (LM-generated keywords, ranked by citation count) and You.com web search restricted to arXiv/PubMed; OA full texts are added, otherwise abstracts only. Bi-encoder retrieval (top 100) then cross-encoder reranking to top N with meta-filtering (max 3 passages/paper, normalized citation counts). Inference: initial cited draft, LM-generated natural-language feedback (max 3), feedback-driven extra retrieval queries, then a 'citation verification' step where the generator checks that citation-worthy statements are supported by retrieved passages and post-hoc inserts citations. This is LM self-verification of its own output, not an independent claim-to-source checker, and there is no DOI/Crossref metadata check (S2 title-existence checking is used only to score baselines). No systematic-review-style title/abstract screening, no audit trail of exclusions, no citation-network analysis, no manuscript import/audit (input is a query string, per Nature task formulation and the demo API model). Verbatim evidence: the retired demo UI (github.com/allenai/openscilm, EvidenceCardContent.tsx) rendered each citation's retrieved snippet in quotation marks; the Citation model carries 'A relevant snippet from the cited paper', so passage-level snippets exist but not claim-aligned quote extraction. Licensing: GitHub API reports Apache-2.0 for AkariAsai/OpenScholar and allenai/openscilm; HF model card text says 'The code and model are released under Apache 2.0' but the card's metadata tag is license: llama3.1 (inconsistency worth flagging); OpenScholar-DataStore-V3 card says license: mit; ScholarQABench data ODC-BY; openscilm_queries CC BY 4.0; Nature paper CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Deployment: self-hosted Python pipeline; run.py imports vllm and sets tensor_parallel_size=torch.cuda.device_count() (CUDA GPU required for local 8B inference); requires S2_API_KEY, optional You.com key, OpenAI key for GPT-4o backend; README says the peS2o index (200+M embeddings) 'requires a lot of CPU memory'; 8B was trained on 8xA100. The public demo URLs openscholar.allen.ai, open-scholar.allen.ai and openscilm.allen.ai all return HTTP 301 to https://asta.allen.ai/ (curl -I, 2026-09-02), i.e. the OpenScholar demo has been folded into Ai2's Asta; the demo repo's AstaBanner reads 'Try Asta, a scholarly research assistant from Ai2'. GitHub repo last pushed 2025-08-13, 1,589 stars. Empirical validation (Nature): ScholarQABench, 2,967 expert-written queries and 208 long-form answers across CS, physics, neuroscience, biomedicine; OS-8B +6.1% correctness vs GPT-4o and +5.5% vs PaperQA2; GPT-4o fabricates citations 78-90% of the time while OpenScholar is on par with experts; OS-GPT-4o +12% over GPT-4o; 16 PhD experts on 108 Scholar-Multi questions preferred OS-8B 51% and OS-GPT-4o 70% vs 32% for GPT-4o; retrieval ablation on Scholar-CS: web-only 45.9 correctness/12.6 citation F1, S2-only 47.9/39.1, combined 49.6/47.6; demo used by >30,000 users with ~90,000 queries. ScholarQABench metrics: rubric-based correctness (GPT-4o-Turbo judge), sentence-level citation precision/recall/F1, Prometheus organization/relevance/coverage. Sources fetched: arxiv.org/abs/2411.14199, arxiv.org/html/2411.14199v1, export.arxiv.org API, api.crossref.org, api.openalex.org, nature.com article, eutils PubMed, github.com/AkariAsai/OpenScholar (+raw README, run.py, retriever/README.md, requirements.txt), api.github.com repo records, github.com/AkariAsai/ScholarQABench (+raw README), huggingface.co/OpenSciLM/Llama-3.1_OpenScholar-8B (+raw card, API), HF datastore V3 and openscilm_queries cards, allenai.org/blog/openscholar, allenai/openscilm raw sources (models.py, open_scholar.py, EvidenceCardContent.tsx, Report.ts, AstaBanner.tsx, DisclaimerModal.tsx), and the three demo hostnames.

STORM.summary: STORM (Stanford OVAL; Shao et al., NAACL 2024, DOI 10.18653/v1/2024.naacl-long.347, Crossref-verified 2026-09-02) is an MIT-licensed, self-hostable Python package (knowledge-storm 1.1.1 on PyPI, released 2025-09-29; repo last pushed 2025-09-30, 31,205 stars per GitHub API on 2026-09-02) that writes Wikipedia-style long-form articles with inline [n] citations from a topic string. Grounding comes exclusively from general web-search APIs (You.com, Bing, Brave, Serper, DuckDuckGo, Tavily, SearXNG, Google, Azure AI Search) or a user-supplied CSV corpus indexed in Qdrant (VectorRM); there is no OpenAlex/Crossref/PubMed/Semantic Scholar connector, the only arXiv retriever in rm.py is documented as '[Alpha] ... for internal use only, not intended for the public', and the optional Wikipedia-derived URL trust filter in retriever.py actually lists arXiv, bioRxiv, medRxiv, SSRN and ResearchGate as GENERALLY_UNRELIABLE (the filter defaults to accept-all in the example runners). STORM automates question/query generation (perspective-guided personas, simulated writer-expert conversations, question-to-query decomposition) rather than helping a user refine a research question; Co-STORM adds user utterances to steer the discourse. It performs no title/abstract relevance screening, keeps no per-record inclusion/exclusion audit trail (it persists conversation_log.json, raw_search_results.json, url_to_info.json and llm_call_history.jsonl), does no citation-network analysis, no DOI/metadata verification, and no in-pipeline claim-to-source verification; the paper only evaluates citation quality offline (Mistral 7B-Instruct judge: citation recall 84.83, precision 85.18). Full text is obtained by downloading search-result web pages with httpx and extracting with trafilatura into ~1000-char snippets, not by OA/DOI PDF retrieval; the Streamlit demo shows these retrieved snippets per reference as 'Highlights' but not claim-level verbatim quotes. It cannot import an externally written manuscript. Deployment: pip install, Python >=3.10, any litellm-supported LLM (OpenAI/Azure or local vLLM/TGI/Ollama), a search-engine API key in secrets.toml, embeddings device cpu/mps/cuda for VectorRM (GPU optional), plus a hosted research preview at storm.genie.stanford.edu. Empirical validation (arXiv PDF fetched 2026-09-02): FreshWiki benchmark of 100 recent Wikipedia articles; automatic article metrics STORM vs oRAG ROUGE-1 45.82 vs 44.26, ROUGE-L 16.70 vs 16.51, entity recall 14.10 vs 12.57; outline heading soft recall 86.26 (GPT-3.5) / 92.73 (GPT-4); human study with 10 experienced Wikipedia editors on 20 article pairs: STORM preferred 26 vs 14, Organization 4.00 vs 3.25 (p=0.005), Verifiability 3.80 vs 3.85 (n.s.); abstract reports +25% absolute organized and +10% broad-coverage articles. All evidence URLs were fetched on 2026-09-02.

Elicit.summary: Elicit (Elicit Research, PBC) is a commercial, closed-source hosted platform for AI-assisted literature search, screening, data extraction, systematic reviews and auto-generated research Reports; included only as a commercial reference point. All evidence fetched 2026-09-02. Data sources: ~138M papers from Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex and PubMed plus ClinicalTrials.gov (support.elicit.com/en/articles/553025). Query refinement: suggests clarifications/angles to the research question and auto-builds keyword queries (elicit.com/blog/introducing-elicit-reports/, elicit.com/blog/introducing-keyword-search, 2025-10-23). Screening: AI title/abstract and full-text screening with auto-suggested criteria and dual review; each decision records exclusion reasons, per-criterion scores and supporting quotes, PRISMA flow diagram and search strategies exportable; Pro/Scale/Enterprise can export screening-recommendation and extraction tables (elicit.com/solutions/systematic-review; elicit.com/blog/systematic-review-for-prisma-2020, 2026-05-06; support.elicit.com/en/articles/1153857). No citation-network/graph feature: API paper object exposes only citedByCount and doi/pmid, with no reference or citing-paper endpoints (docs.elicit.com). Full text: OA papers fetched automatically; paywalled papers via browser extension using institutional logins/EZProxy, otherwise title+abstract only (support.elicit.com/en/articles/553025, /6123329). Drafting: Reports are auto-generated research briefs with sentence-level exact quotes and editable paper sets, exportable to PDF/Word; no manuscript editor, and Elicit advises against pasting its output verbatim (support.elicit.com/en/articles/14757952). No documented Crossref/DOI verification, post-hoc claim verifier, or external-manuscript audit; uploads serve chat/extraction only. Licensing: proprietary ToS (last updated 2023-09-12); deployment hosted-only, API key with Pro+ plan, 100 req/min/IP, MCP endpoint, Enterprise single-tenancy; pricing Basic free, Pro $49/user/mo, Scale $169/user/mo (elicit.com/pricing). Empirical validation (vendor, elicit.com/blog/evaluating-elicit-slr): 994 Cochrane reviews / 38,493 records; 95.0% search recall, 96.9% sensitivity / 92.5% specificity abstract screening, 99.5% full-text recall with 94.8% per-criterion accuracy, 95.6% extraction on Methods/Participants/Interventions; Reports eval (elicit.com/blog/elicit-reports-eval/): 17 PhD evaluators, 29 Elicit vs 120 competitor reports, several tools statistically equivalent. Independent (Crossref-verified): Hilkenmeier et al. 2025 SSCR, 10.1177/08944393251404052, 81.4% extraction accuracy vs 86.7% human (n.s.), 43 studies/602 data points; Lagisz et al. 2026 RSM, 10.1017/rsm.2026.10080, 70/90 prompts >87% accuracy, 90% value agreement across accounts but supporting quotes matched only 46%. Canonical citation is Elicit's official @software URL citation with no DOI, so crossref_verified=false.
